claims.text: Designing a specific eutectic phase distribution will increase the strength of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Designing a specific eutectic phase distribution will increase the ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Controlled solidification can produce a refined eutectic microstructure with an optimized phase distribution.
Controlled cooling rates during solidification promote the desired refined microstructure.
Eutectic phase distribution and grain size mediate the proposed changes in mechanical properties.
A refined microstructure with a balanced distribution of hard and ductile phases enhances load-bearing capacity.
A balanced distribution of hard and ductile phases permits plastic deformation while retaining load-bearing capacity.
The refined microstructure will increase yield strength by approximately 20% relative to the conventional microstructure.
The refined microstructure will increase ductility by approximately 15% relative to the conventional microstructure.
The proposed improvement is limited to controlled-solidification conditions and suitable alloy compositions typical of structural applications.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility improvements may vary with alloy composition and solidification parameters.
